title: Applied Scientist
summary: Applied scientist and AI engineer with 8+ years designing, implementing and evaluating ML and LLM solutions from prototype to production, with an MSc in Machine Learning and AI. Builds LangGraph multi-agent systems, agentic tools and RAG applications in Python, and designs automated LLM evaluation with evaluators, tracing and failure detection. Works closely with software engineers to take modelling solutions into production with FastAPI, Docker and MLflow. Alongside this, I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD.

project.name: Cloud Agent Benchmark Suite
bullets: Built a benchmark of cloud engineering tasks measuring how LLM coding agents use tools and documentation, with a LangGraph harness running Claude and open models in sandboxed environments.
Scored runs with automated checks and LLM evaluators, traced failures to find where agents struggled, and exposed the harness through a Dockerized FastAPI service for repeatable runs.

paragraphs: I am applying for the Applied Scientist role on the AWS Developer Tools Science team. My recent work has been building LLM agents and, just as much, measuring them: evaluation pipelines, tracing and failure analysis for agents running in production. The thread through my career is applied ML that has to prove itself on real problems.

Your team builds agents and benchmarks for developers working on AWS, and knowing whether an agent is actually good is the question I find most interesting right now. It is also a personal move. My fiancée lives in Berlin, and I am building my career in the city where we are making our home.

I would bring practical evaluation experience. At United Health Group I built evaluation and observability pipelines for Question Answering and Summary Agents that reduced human-in-the-loop review by 43%, and a LangGraph multi-agent analytics chatbot that cut manual analysis by 98%. Designing honest benchmarks for agents on cloud workloads feels like the natural next step.

Outside work I am building ThinkTree.AI, a non-profit AI learning platform used by NGO teachers to support students with ADHD. It has taught me to test tools with the people who use them, not just in a notebook. I would be glad to talk about how I could contribute to your team.
